newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia still studying new mining rules -officia.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia still studying new mining rules -officia.

text.p: Indonesia is still studying new mining rules, which include requiring foreign firms to allocate a 10-percent stake in their ventures to the government.
"The new mining rules are still being studied. We need time before they can be implemented," a Mines and Energy Ministry official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters on Wednesday.
The official said the government would also tighten existing rules, especially on the announcement of new finds and share divestment to local firms.
"The Busang case has caused the government to be careful," he said, referring to the biggest mining swindle in history.

Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd said its Busang property in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province contained some 71 million ounces of gold, making it the biggest discovery this century.
An independent audit, however, found it was almost worthless and that data had been falsified on an unprecedented scale.
